MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The SanDisk 32GB two-pack fits my repeated purchases of SanDisk cards in familiar capacities; spare cards feel like a useful continuation of what I already buy.",
    "The 64GB card and reader bundle recognizes my recurring need for removable storage, although the reader adds less value because I already bought a UGREEN reader."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "The Fire tablet, streaming sticks and Kindle suggest new devices when my purchases mostly support equipment I already own; owning a Fire 7 does not mean I currently want another screen.",
    "Echo Auto relates to my car purchases only loosely: my mounts and cables solve physical connection needs, while a voice assistant serves a different purpose. The Echo lighting kit and AirPods also lack a clear connection to a current need.",
    "The 256GB card matches my interest in storage, but its much higher capacity and speed are not benefits I have shown a need for, and I would need to confirm compatibility."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My Fire tablet purchase seems to have been taken as interest in a broad range of Amazon devices, even though my follow-up purchases were practical accessories.",
    "My memory-card purchases seem to suggest that any storage upgrade will appeal, but familiar capacities and a clear use matter more to me than larger specifications."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "I repeatedly buy useful accessories such as cables, mounts, card holders and power strips, and my latest purchase was a replacement lens cap; those purchases suggest ongoing equipment upkeep.",
    "What I already own matters: another reader overlaps with my existing reader, while spare memory cards can still be useful because I have bought them repeatedly.",
    "Compatibility with my existing equipment matters more than a broad connection to electronics, cameras or car accessories."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations recognized my recurring storage needs but read my device ownership as interest in new gadgets rather than practical support for equipment I already use."
}
